To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
serum IgA responses are induced after pertussis infections and that they provide an additional role for pertuss is diagnostics.

1) IgA responses against pertussis antigens are induced after infection, 2) IgA levels against PT, FHA and Prn are significantly higher after infection compared with healthy children, 3) IgA levels for PT, FHA and/or Prn are significantly correlated with IgG levels in infected and wP-vaccinated children, 4) high numbers of IgA memory B-cells are found after infection and wP and aPP vaccination.
serum IgA responses to the three main pertussis vaccine components are significantly higher in infected than in healthy children, but that high IgA levels are induced by wP and aPC vaccines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to improve pertussis diagnostics in vaccinated individuals.
the role of serum IgA in the diagnosis of pertussis in vaccinated and infected children.
the development of a diagnostic test for the detection of recent pertussis infections in vaccinated children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
serum IgA levels against PT, FHA and Prn are not useful for diagnosing pertusssis in healthy children who have received an aP vaccine.
IgA responses are of diagnostic value for recent pertusssis infection, but only in the absence of high IgG levels induced by wP or a P vaccinations.
serum IgA responses to PT are useful in diagnosing pertusis in vaccinated individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of IgA-ELISPOT for pertussis diagnostics is not recommended.
serum IgA responses to PT, FHA and Prn provide additional diagnostic value in children vaccinated with wP or a booster vaccination with aP, but not in children who have been primed with aP.
serum IgA levels against PT can be used as a diagnostic tool in vaccinated children.
The main takeaway from our work is that
serum IgA responses are a promising tool for the diagnosis of pertussis in vaccinated children, but the role of these responses in protection is largely unknown.
the use of serum IgA-ELISAs for the diagnosis of pertussis in vaccinated children is not warranted.
serum IgA-anti-PT levels can be used as a diagnostic tool in pertussis.
